steps.what: Count collected tickets at this door.
Name the door, performance and stub number.
Record ticket count v1 in the ticketing system.
Check ticket count v1 quotes the door and stub number.

tasks.design: She counts the collected tickets and names the door, the performance and the stub number. A separate step records ticket count v1 in the ticketing system ({OTHER}). She checks that version against the stubs. The count is not sent, no mismatch alert is raised, and the record does not time her.
tasks.previous_blocker: The stub total was written on the envelope after the count, so there was no standing record to check against the pile.
tasks.enabler_now: A ticketing screen can file door, performance and stub number from the number she has already named, and hold that version until she checks it.
tasks.still_hard: A torn stub, a door with no named performance, or a dark aisle still needs her eyes and her count.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which stubs were actually collected, and refusing a number she did not count.
tasks.altitude: She still counts every stub and names the door, the performance and the number. She checks ticket count v1 before it stands. She stops copying a number she has already named. She does not gain a right to let a gate scan replace the pile, or to file a count she has not checked.

reach.task: Open the performance the stubs belong to
reach.learn: Which performance is already open, so a blank show is not filled with a guessed count.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge, not a measured study of this firm: counting collected tickets by hand is the bulk of this task. Recording a door, a performance and a stub number she has already named is the small slice.
Works-council consent is required before logs are used to watch staff. This ticket count records door, performance and stub number. It does not log her speed or her hours.
No high-risk area in Annex III applies to this group. This ticket count does not score her or decide who may enter.

assumptions: She counts the stubs herself. The ticketing system may already store gate scans from the box office, outside this task. This task does not read those scans and does not treat a scan total as the collected count. That scan record is not counted as saved.

In the name step she records door, performance and stub number. That capture stays at full time. If any of those is missing, the file step does not run and she writes the number on the stub envelope as she does today.

Ticket count v1 is filed only after she has named those fields. She then checks that version against the stubs. A change after the check voids the file. There is no send of the count, to a colleague or to anyone outside. No mismatch alert is raised.
The record stores door, performance and stub number. It does not store her hours, her speed, or a location trail.
unknowns: Whether the box office, rather than the usher, writes the stub total today.
Whether each performance is already named before she counts.
research_questions: Which of door, performance and stub number does she already name before anyone writes the total?

incremental.description: When the filed door or stub number is wrong, correct ticket count v1 before it stands.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is a night of unnamed doors or a dark pile, so she writes the number on the envelope and the file does not run. High is 4, only recording ticket count v1 after she has named the door, the performance and the stub number and has checked that version. Counting and naming stay.

steps.what: Read exhibit facts from the house guide.
Lead tours and answer visitors' questions about the exhibits.

tasks.design: A separate step reads exhibit name and one public sentence from the house guide ({OTHER}) when the curator has already written them. She still leads the tours and answers visitors' questions herself. No script is sent, and no chatbot answers for her.
tasks.previous_blocker: The public sentence lived on a wall label or in a guide she carried, and the answer still had to be spoken to the visitor in front of the exhibit.
tasks.enabler_now: A house guide can show the exhibit name and one public sentence the curator already wrote, before she starts the tour.
tasks.still_hard: A visitor's question, a closed room, and the pace of the group stay with her.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing the question the visitor actually asked, and stopping when the public sentence does not fit.
tasks.altitude: She still leads every tour and answers every question. The house guide does not speak for her. She does not gain a right to send a script to a visitor.

reach.task: Write the public sentence for an exhibit
reach.learn: Which exhibit already has a public sentence, and which wall label she must use when it is blank.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge, not a measured study of this firm: leading the tour and answering visitors is almost all of this task. Looking up a sentence the curator already wrote is the small slice, and only when that sentence exists.
Works-council consent is required before logs are used to watch staff. This house-guide read shows an exhibit name and one public sentence. It does not log her speed or her hours.
No high-risk area in Annex III applies to this group. Reading a public sentence does not score her or grade the visitor.

assumptions: The curator maintains exhibit name and one public sentence on the house guide, outside this task. That upkeep is not counted as saved. If either field is blank, the read step does not run and she uses the wall label. The tour stays at full time either way.
She leads the tour and answers the questions. That talk with visitors stays hers. No answer is drafted for her, no chatbot speaks, and no script is sent to a visitor or to a colleague.
The house-guide read does not log her speed or her hours. No alert is raised when a sentence is missing.
unknowns: Whether a curator writes a public sentence before the season.
Whether someone else, rather than the usher, leads the tour.
research_questions: Which exhibits already have a public sentence, and which still have only a wall label?

incremental.description: Tell the curator when a public sentence does not match the exhibit in front of the group.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is a tour whose exhibits have no public sentence, so the read is empty and she uses the wall label. High is 1, only that lookup, when the curator already wrote the exhibit name and one public sentence. Leading the tour and answering visitors stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Count artist merchandise for the stand inventory.
Name each item and the quantity on hand.
File merchandise count v1 in the shop till.
Check merchandise count v1 quotes the items and quantities.
Sell artist merchandise and complete the sale.

tasks.design: She counts the stand and names each item and quantity. A separate step files merchandise count v1 in the shop till ({OTHER}), and she checks that version. She still sells the artist merchandise and takes payment herself. No receipt is emailed, and no stock alert is raised.
tasks.previous_blocker: The stand was counted by eye and the sale was taken in the same breath, so the quantity on hand was not a version anyone could check.
tasks.enabler_now: A shop till can file item and quantity from the lines she has already named, and hold that version until she checks it.
tasks.still_hard: A visitor choosing a print, a cash payment, and a pile that was moved during the show still need her.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing what is actually left on the stand, and refusing a quantity she did not count.
tasks.altitude: She still counts the stand, names every item and quantity, and sells the merchandise herself. She checks merchandise count v1 before it stands. She does not gain a right to let the till choose the count, or to send a receipt she has not been asked to send.

reach.task: Pay for artist merchandise at the stand
reach.learn: Which items she still sells by hand when the count record is blank.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge, not a measured study of this firm: counting the stand and selling to the visitor are the bulk of this task. Filing item and quantity she has already named is the small slice.
Works-council consent is required before logs are used to watch staff. This merchandise count records item and quantity. It does not log her speed or her hours.
No high-risk area in Annex III applies to this group. This merchandise count does not score her or price the sale.

assumptions: She counts the stand herself. Item names on the shop till, if any, are maintained by the shop lead outside this task and are not counted as saved. She still names item and quantity from the count.
In the name step she records item and quantity. That capture stays at full time. If either is missing, the file step does not run and she notes the count on paper as she does today.

Merchandise count v1 is filed first. She then checks that version against the items and quantities she named. A change after the check voids the file. There is no send of the count. The sale and the payment stay in person and are not a filed version. No receipt is emailed. No stock alert is raised.
The count stores item and quantity. It does not store her hours or her speed.
unknowns: Whether a shop lead, rather than the usher, counts the stand.
Whether payment is taken on a till or only by cash.
research_questions: Which of item and quantity does she already name before anyone writes the stand total?

incremental.description: When a filed quantity does not match the stand, correct merchandise count v1 before it stands.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is a stand she notes on paper because item or quantity is missing, so the file does not run. High is 4, only filing merchandise count v1 after she has named item and quantity and has checked that version. Counting, naming and the sale stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Hear which volunteer staff can work.
Assign each volunteer usher a door and a start time.
File the schedule as usher roster v1.
Check usher roster v1 quotes the doors and start times.
Send usher roster v1 to the volunteer corps.
Direct the volunteer corps at their doors.

tasks.design: She hears who can work and assigns each volunteer usher a door and a start time. A separate step files usher roster v1 on the {CALENDAR}, she checks that version, and a further step sends only that version to the volunteer corps by {EMAIL}. Directing them at the door stays hers. The roster is not sent outside the organisation, and it does not log speed or hours.
tasks.previous_blocker: The doors were assigned in the room and then retold by mouth, so there was no roster version to check before people were told.
tasks.enabler_now: A calendar can file person, door and start time from the assignments she has already made, and mail that version to the corps after she checks it.
tasks.still_hard: A volunteer who swaps at the door, a dark house, and who can cover a late arrival stay with her.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing who can actually stand that door, and refusing a roster line she did not assign.
tasks.altitude: She still hears who can work, assigns every door, and directs the corps in the house. She checks usher roster v1 before it is sent to colleagues. She does not gain a right to let a list choose the doors, or to send a roster she has not checked.

reach.task: Work the door named on the roster
reach.learn: Which volunteers still need a spoken direction after the roster is sent.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge, not a measured study of this firm: hearing who can work, assigning doors and directing the corps are the bulk of this task. Filing and sending a roster she has already assigned is the small slice.
Works-council consent is required before logs are used to watch staff. This roster records person, door and start time. It does not log her speed or her hours.
No high-risk area in Annex III applies to this group. This roster does not score a volunteer or decide who is hired.

assumptions: She hears availability and assigns door and start time herself. A volunteer list, if one exists on the calendar, is not treated as free: the hearing and the assignment stay at full time. If person, door or start time is missing, the file and the send do not run and she tells people in the room as she does today.

Usher roster v1 is filed first. She then checks that version against the person, door and start time she assigned. The send transmits only that checked version to the volunteer corps. A change after the check voids the file and the send. The send is to colleagues. It is not a send outside the organisation.
Directing volunteers at the door is spoken and stays at full time. It is not a second send and it does not file a version.
The roster stores person, door and start time. It does not log speed, hours worked, or a location trail. No absence alert is raised.
unknowns: Whether a coordinator, rather than the usher, writes the roster today.
Whether volunteers read mail before they arrive.
research_questions: Which of person, door and start time does she already assign before anyone is told?

incremental.description: When a volunteer swaps after the send, void usher roster v1 and assign the door again.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is a night she assigns in the room and never files, so the send does not run. High is 6, only filing and sending usher roster v1 after she has assigned person, door and start time and has checked that version. Hearing, assigning and directing stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still counts every stub, leads every tour, sells the merchandise and takes the payment, and assigns and directs the volunteer corps. The ticket count, the merchandise count and the roster do not choose those acts. She does not gain a right to file a count she has not made, or to send a roster she has not checked.
reach: box office (which performance is already open)
curator (which exhibit sentence is already on the house guide)
visitor (which items she still sells by hand)
volunteer usher (which door still needs a spoken direction)
skills_to_grow: Refuse ticket count v1 until the stub number is one she counted.
Treat a blank house guide as a blank and use the wall label.
Refuse a send of usher roster v1 until she has checked that version.
role.ambitious_version: She files the stub count the same night, and the roster only after she has assigned the doors. The tour, the sale and the direction of volunteers stay hers. No unchecked roster goes to the corps.
